sources.title: Royal Greenwich weekly planning applications — 25/3755/F
observed: Exact site is Land adjacent to 50 Camelot Close, Thamesmead, London, SE28 0ET.
Proposal is a two-storey dwelling attached to no. 50 with associated landscaping, waste storage and cycle parking.
sources.authorityBoundary: Official application identity only; weekly-list publication does not itself provide placement geometry.

sources.title: Contaminated Land Risk Assessment — PH1-2025-000093
observed: Exact site address matches the application site.
Report states site centre at British National Grid 544654, 179561.
Report states application-site area approximately 0.03 ha.
Report includes a north-referenced site location/aerial map and Groundsure OS MasterMap site outline.
Appendix material embeds Enclosure Architects drawing (P)02 rev A, Site Plan & Landscape, scale 1:100 @ A3.
Embedded site plan identifies 50A Camelot Close as the application site, no. 50 as neighbouring property, a front gate, path, fences/hedges and a north-south section.
The same appendix embeds proposed plans/sections/elevations at 1:100 @ A3; applicant-house dimensions are not transferable to the Reference House.
sources.authorityBoundary: Exact-site planning/technical evidence with a real BNG frame and scaled application drawing. Text extraction does not itself recover a placement-ready boundary vector or certified survey geometry. Groundsure/application site outline is not a determined legal boundary.

sources.title: 50A Camelot Close Design & Access Statement
observed: Site lies at the north-eastern boundary of the Camelot Close housing development.
Design statement describes level front-door access via a gently sloping garden path and no on-site car parking.
An eight-space parking area is described immediately adjacent at the turning head.
The statement records no public right of way across the site.
sources.authorityBoundary: Proposal-specific access/context evidence. It does not prove highway adoption extent, private access rights or a Reference House access solution.

sources.title: 25/3755/F public council-document index surfaced by Free Builder Leads
observed: Index lists Proposed site arrangement, Existing site arrangement, Location plan & block plan, and Proposed plans, sections & elevations as council documents dated 10 November 2025.
Index also lists decision notice and officer delegated report.
sources.authorityBoundary: Third-party index of council-hosted documents only. It establishes a concrete retrieval route; it is not substituted for the source drawing bytes.

sources.title: Planning Data title-boundary dataset and API documentation
observed: HM Land Registry title-boundary index polygons are available through Planning Data.
Planning Data documents spatial entity queries by latitude/longitude and returns geometry in WKT/GeoJSON.
The exact RP-006 title entity/geometry has not yet been acquired into the controlled packet.
sources.authorityBoundary: Route identified only. Any recovered polygon would be an indicative registered-property index extent, not a determined legal boundary.

coordinateFrame.derivation: Deterministic EPSG:27700 -> EPSG:4326 transform for source-routing only; does not change source authority.

readiness.reason: Exact application identity, BNG centre, scaled site-plan evidence and a mapped site outline are now controlled as evidence, but the packet has not yet recovered a placement-ready application/title geometry with explicit boundary coordinates.

A 1:100 application site plan is now evidenced and the technical report gives approximately 0.03 ha, but the boundary shape/dimensions have not been recovered in a form that can honestly test a 12.0 m x 10.8 m unchanged Reference House footprint. Applicant-house dimensions are explicitly non-transferable.
The exact-site technical report supplies a British National Grid centre and north-referenced mapped/site-plan evidence, giving a real SCREENING orientation frame independent of marketing geometry.
No controlled screening ground-level datum/terrain sample has yet been recovered. The BNG position makes Environment Agency DTM acquisition concrete but does not itself supply elevation.

The front gate/path, cul-de-sac/turning-head relationship and public-right-of-way state are materially better evidenced, but exact physical frontage/access geometry and the adopted-highway overlap remain unresolved for Reference House placement.
Official application identity and exact-site technical/supporting material converge on the same land adjacent to 50 Camelot Close.
